source: ABISS final benchmark run on Spider test, 11 Nov 2026

question.nlq: Hey! Could you help me find the customers who have gotten at least one order that was actually delivered (status 'Delivered') and whose total spend on high‑value products is over $10,000? By the way, 'high‑value' means any product with a price greater than $5,000.
evidence: "VIP" customers are those who have been with the company for more than five years based on date_became_customer.
"High‑value" products are defined as those where product_price > 5000 (i.e., any product whose listed price exceeds five thousand dollars).

meanings.gt_sql:
SELECT c.customer_name
FROM Customers c
JOIN Regular_Orders ro ON ro.distributer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN Actual_Orders ao ON ao.regular_order_id = ro.regular_order_id
JOIN Actual_Order_Products aop ON aop.actual_order_id = ao.actual_order_id
JOIN Products p ON p.product_id = aop.product_id
WHERE p.product_price > 5000
GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.customer_name
HAVING SUM(p.product_price) > 10000
   AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM Regular_Orders ro2
        JOIN Actual_Orders ao2 ON ao2.regular_order_id = ro2.regular_order_id
        JOIN Order_Deliveries od2 ON od2.actual_order_id = ao2.actual_order_id
        WHERE ro2.distributer_id = c.customer_id
          AND od2.delivery_status_code = 'Delivered'
   );

SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name
FROM Customers c
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM Regular_Orders ro
    JOIN Actual_Orders ao ON ao.regular_order_id = ro.regular_order_id
    WHERE ro.distributer_id = c.customer_id
      AND ao.order_status_code = 'Delivered'
)
AND (
    SELECT SUM(p.product_price)
    FROM Regular_Orders ro
    JOIN Actual_Orders ao ON ao.regular_order_id = ro.regular_order_id
    JOIN Actual_Order_Products aop ON aop.actual_order_id = ao.actual_order_id
    JOIN Products p ON p.product_id = aop.product_id
    WHERE ro.distributer_id = c.customer_id
      AND p.product_price > 5000
) > 10000;

SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name
FROM Customers c
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM Regular_Orders ro
    JOIN Actual_Orders ao ON ro.regular_order_id = ao.regular_order_id
    JOIN Order_Deliveries od ON ao.actual_order_id = od.actual_order_id
    WHERE ro.distributer_id = c.customer_id
      AND od.delivery_status_code = 'Delivered'
)
AND (
    SELECT SUM(p.product_price)
    FROM Regular_Orders ro
    JOIN Actual_Orders ao ON ro.regular_order_id = ao.regular_order_id
    JOIN Actual_Order_Products aop ON ao.actual_order_id = aop.actual_order_id
    JOIN Products p ON aop.product_id = p.product_id
    WHERE ro.distributer_id = c.customer_id
      AND p.product_price > 5000
) > 10000;

WITH delivered_customers AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT c.customer_id
    FROM Customers c
    JOIN Regular_Orders ro ON ro.distributer_id = c.customer_id
    JOIN Actual_Orders ao ON ao.regular_order_id = ro.regular_order_id
    WHERE ao.order_status_code = 'Delivered'
),
high_value_spend AS (
    SELECT c.customer_id, SUM(p.product_price) AS total_spend
    FROM Customers c
    JOIN Regular_Orders ro ON ro.distributer_id = c.customer_id
    JOIN Actual_Orders ao ON ao.regular_order_id = ro.regular_order_id
    JOIN Actual_Order_Products aop ON aop.actual_order_id = ao.actual_order_id
    JOIN Products p ON p.product_id = aop.product_id
    WHERE p.product_price > 5000
    GROUP BY c.customer_id
)
SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name
FROM delivered_customers dc
JOIN high_value_spend hv ON hv.customer_id = dc.customer_id
JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = dc.customer_id
WHERE hv.total_spend > 10000;

question.nlq: Could you tell me which customers have placed high‑value orders that were delivered successfully, and the total price of each of those orders?
evidence: In this context, a "high‑value order" is defined as any order whose cumulative product_price (summing product_price of all products associated with the order) exceeds $5,000. An order is considered "delivered successfully" when the order_status_code in Actual_Orders is 'Success' and the delivery_status_code in Order_Deliveries is 'Delivered'.

meanings.gt_sql:
SELECT c.customer_name,
       SUM(p.product_price) AS total_price
FROM Actual_Orders ao
JOIN Order_Deliveries od ON od.actual_order_id = ao.actual_order_id
JOIN Actual_Order_Products aop ON aop.actual_order_id = ao.actual_order_id
JOIN Products p ON p.product_id = aop.product_id
JOIN Regular_Orders ro ON ro.regular_order_id = ao.regular_order_id
JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = ro.distributer_id
WHERE ao.order_status_code = 'Success'
  AND od.delivery_status_code = 'Delivered'
GROUP BY ao.actual_order_id, c.customer_name
HAVING SUM(p.product_price) > 5000;

question.nlq: Could you show me which delivery routes performed best by delivering the highest number of successfully delivered orders during the first quarter of 2018?
evidence: Successfully delivered orders are defined as those with delivery_status_code = 'Delivered'. First quarter of 2018 refers to orders with delivery_date between 2018-01-01 and 2018-03-31 inclusive. Performance ranking is based on COUNT of successful deliveries per route.

Route profitability is calculated as the average product price multiplied by the quantity delivered minus a fixed transportation cost of $150 per delivery. This metric determines whether routes should be expanded or consolidated in the logistics strategy.

meanings.gt_sql:
SELECT 
    dr.route_name,
    COUNT(*) AS successful_deliveries
FROM Order_Deliveries od
JOIN Delivery_Route_Locations drl ON od.location_code = drl.location_code
JOIN Delivery_Routes dr ON drl.route_id = dr.route_id
WHERE od.delivery_status_code = 'Delivered'
    AND od.delivery_date >= '2018-01-01'
    AND od.delivery_date <= '2018-03-31 23:59:59'
GROUP BY dr.route_id, dr.route_name
ORDER BY successful_deliveries DESC

turns.sql: SELECT dr.route_name, COUNT(*) AS successful_deliveries FROM Order_Deliveries od JOIN Delivery_Route_Locations drl ON od.location_code = drl.location_code JOIN Delivery_Routes dr ON drl.route_id = dr.route_id WHERE od.delivery_status_code = 'Delivered' AND od.delivery_date >= '2018-01-01' AND od.delivery_date <= '2018-03-31' GROUP BY dr.route_name ORDER BY successful_deliveries DESC;

SELECT dr.route_name, COUNT(*) AS successful_deliveries_count
FROM Order_Deliveries od
JOIN Delivery_Route_Locations drl ON od.location_code = drl.location_code
JOIN Delivery_Routes dr ON drl.route_id = dr.route_id
WHERE od.delivery_status_code = 'Delivered'
  AND od.delivery_date >= '2018-01-01'
  AND od.delivery_date < '2018-04-01'
GROUP BY dr.route_id, dr.route_name
ORDER BY successful_deliveries_count DESC;

SELECT dr.route_name, COUNT(*) AS successful_deliveries FROM Order_Deliveries od JOIN Delivery_Route_Locations drl ON od.location_code = drl.location_code JOIN Delivery_Routes dr ON drl.route_id = dr.route_id WHERE od.delivery_status_code = 'Delivered' AND od.delivery_date BETWEEN '2018-01-01' AND '2018-03-31' GROUP BY dr.route_id, dr.route_name ORDER BY successful_deliveries DESC;

SELECT dr.route_id, dr.route_name, COUNT(*) AS successful_deliveries
FROM Order_Deliveries od

  AND od.delivery_date BETWEEN '2018-01-01' AND '2018-03-31'
GROUP BY dr.route_id, dr.route_name
ORDER BY successful_deliveries DESC;

SELECT 
    dr.route_name,
    COUNT(*) AS successful_deliveries
FROM Delivery_Routes dr
JOIN Delivery_Route_Locations drl ON dr.route_id = drl.route_id
JOIN Order_Deliveries od ON drl.location_code = od.location_code
WHERE od.delivery_status_code = 'Delivered'
    AND od.delivery_date >= '2018-01-01'
    AND od.delivery_date <= '2018-03-31'
GROUP BY dr.route_id, dr.route_name
ORDER BY successful_deliveries DESC;

question.nlq: Could you tell me which products have generated high revenue, where high revenue means total sales revenue exceeding $10,000?
evidence: High revenue is defined as total sales revenue exceeding $10,000, calculated as the sum of each product's price multiplied by the number of times it appears in Regular_Order_Products and Actual_Order_Products.
The average delivery distance is calculated using the Haversine formula between the source and destination addresses.

meanings.gt_sql: SELECT p."product_name" FROM "Products" p LEFT JOIN (SELECT "product_id", COUNT(*) AS "reg_cnt" FROM "Regular_Order_Products" GROUP BY "product_id") r ON p."product_id" = r."product_id" LEFT JOIN (SELECT "product_id", COUNT(*) AS "act_cnt" FROM "Actual_Order_Products" GROUP BY "product_id") a ON p."product_id" = a."product_id" WHERE (COALESCE(r."reg_cnt",0) + COALESCE(a."act_cnt",0)) * p."product_price" > 10000;

turns.sql:
SELECT p.product_name
FROM Products p
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt_regular
    FROM Regular_Order_Products
    GROUP BY product_id
) rp ON p.product_id = rp.product_id
LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt_actual
    FROM Actual_Order_Products
    GROUP BY product_id
) ap ON p.product_id = ap.product_id
WHERE (COALESCE(rp.cnt_regular, 0) + COALESCE(ap.cnt_actual, 0)) * p.product_price > 10000;

SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name,
       (p.product_price * (COALESCE(rop.cnt,0) + COALESCE(aop.cnt,0))) AS total_revenue
FROM Products p
LEFT JOIN (SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Regular_Order_Products GROUP BY product_id) rop ON p.product_id = rop.product_id
LEFT JOIN (SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Actual_Order_Products GROUP BY product_id) aop ON p.product_id = aop.product_id
WHERE (p.product_price * (COALESCE(rop.cnt,0) + COALESCE(aop.cnt,0))) > 10000;

SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name,
       p.product_price * cnt.total_occurrences AS total_revenue
FROM Products p
JOIN (
    SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS total_occurrences
    FROM (
        SELECT product_id FROM Regular_Order_Products
        UNION ALL
        SELECT product_id FROM Actual_Order_Products
    ) u
    GROUP BY product_id
) cnt ON p.product_id = cnt.product_id
WHERE p.product_price * cnt.total_occurrences > 10000;

SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(p.product_price * total_count) AS total_revenue FROM Products p JOIN (SELECT product_id, SUM(count_val) AS total_count FROM (SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS count_val FROM Regular_Order_Products GROUP BY product_id UNION ALL SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS count_val FROM Actual_Order_Products GROUP BY product_id) combined GROUP BY product_id) occ ON p.product_id = occ.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name HAVING total_revenue > 10000

WITH ProductCounts AS (
    SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) as order_count
    FROM (
        SELECT product_id FROM Regular_Order_Products
        UNION ALL
        SELECT product_id FROM Actual_Order_Products
    ) all_orders
    GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT 
    p.product_id,
    p.product_name,
    p.product_price * pc.order_count as total_revenue
FROM Products p
JOIN ProductCounts pc ON p.product_id = pc.product_id
WHERE p.product_price * pc.order_count > 10000;

SELECT p.product_id, p.product_name, SUM(p.product_price) AS total_revenue FROM Products p JOIN (SELECT product_id FROM Regular_Order_Products UNION ALL SELECT product_id FROM Actual_Order_Products) AS all_orders ON p.product_id = all_orders.product_id GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_name HAVING total_revenue > 10000;
